videos.script: October 2025 sold 0.7 per cent less than October 2024. Every other month of the year grew. {{october}} By Monday, everybody at Varanda had a reason. The rain. A competitor's sale. The economy. Each of them sounded right, and none had been checked. This lesson is about checking. {{tree}} First you break the number down: by channel, by store, into orders and average ticket. The fall turns out to sit in one place. The stores grew. The online shop lost 580 orders, at the same ticket. {{sheet}} You put October in a sheet and measure how much each line moved the total. {{suspects}} Then you write down every suspect before testing any: the calendar, prices, stock, the data itself, and campaigns. One survives. {{cause}} Last, the hardest part. Two things moving together is not one causing the other. You learn to write a finding that says what was checked, what it is consistent with, and what is still open.
